c.st: UEFA and its national associations will not participate in FIFA competitions
c.x:
In the Dictator's Handbook the authors argued that FIFA and IOC function similar to autocratic dictatorships because there is a small group of people who are essential to power. Therefore it is rational to buy them rather than do the right thing by the fans (who have very little power). As cold as the reasoning is, the explanation stuck with me.

Their suggestion is to open up the power structure, e.g. to all past players/Olympians.

c.st: Gas Leak in the Baltic Sea
c.x:
“The Dictator’s Handbook” is a great book that argues (convincingly) that countries “act” not in their “own” self-interest but in the self-interest of their leader.

Which is always to stay in power (and maximize their power).

So I agree as short-sighted and bad it would be for Russia to do this, if it helps Putin stay in power right now, it makes sense.

And honestly, who else would do it?

c.st: Ask HN: First startup / cold feet. Any advice ?
c.x:
I didn't fail my first time. And you're not guaranteed to fail by any means so please don't let anyone convince you of that.

I have never recommended a Paul Graham essay on this site (something that I'll never be able to claim again), but I highly recommend you read this one:

"How Not to Die" (August 2007)
http://www.paulgraham.com/die.html

This has got to be, in my opinion, my 2nd favorite PG essay, right after the 'How Not to Die' essay.

So here in sum is how determination seems to work: it consists of willfulness balanced with discipline, aimed by ambition.

The essay is probably meant to help investors pick good investments. But I say that founders can use it to help pick good co-founders, as well as improve themselves. I would love to read more on things/characteristics about a person that might give evidence of a person's willfulness,…
